matched_pool_nn_notes.construction: each draw partitions the window's incumbents into disjoint reference pool R, probe, and pseudo-newcomer sets, |probe|=|pseudo|=|newcomers|; newcomers and probe both query R (same pool, same size) -> observed delta; pseudo and probe both query R -> the permutation null in this corpus's own embedding geometry
matched_pool_nn_notes.draws: 500. At 40 draws the two-sided permutation p has a FLOOR of 2/40 = 0.05, which the issue-4 window hit exactly; 500 draws resolves it.
matched_pool_nn_notes.floors: the Vendi-based parity/union cells keep the standing m>=100 floor; the NN cell runs to m>=50 because its permutation null widens automatically as m shrinks. The issue-4 window (m=76) is BELOW the Vendi floor and is flagged below_standing_vendi_floor in the cell itself. This is a deliberate bypass for this instrument, not a lowered floor for all of them.
matched_pool_nn_notes.supersedes: the asymmetric construction (newcomers vs ALL incumbents, incumbents vs HALF), which issue #3 omitted rather than report. Measured over 500 half-splits it reads delta -0.0046 [-0.0074,-0.0013] on issue #3's window - negative, band excluding zero, i.e. newcomers CLOSER to incumbents than incumbents are to each other, a spurious echo reading - where the matched construction reads +0.0124. Bias -0.017 (issue-3 window) and -0.0135 (issue-4 window); the synthetic null puts it at -0.030.
matched_pool_nn_notes.legacy_second_defect: as originally written the legacy baseline used ONE random half-split, so its delta carried no band and moved ~0.005 between runs; the published comparison repeats the split 500 times so the bias estimate is stable.
matched_pool_nn_notes.validation: analysis/weather_nn_validate.py, runnable, CPU-only: matched null centres on ~0 in every regime (+0.0006 / +0.0002 / +0.0004); matched delta ~0 under both nulls (p=0.25, 0.28) and +0.594 (p=0.0) when queries occupy directions the reference pool never does; the legacy construction reads -0.0297 and -0.0299 under those same true nulls.
